Incapacitation under desistance and replacement

Source: R/corr.R
incapr.Rd

Crimes prevented by a sentence of s periods served from career age t0, when the offending rate falls with career age and a share r of the crimes prevented is committed by someone else instead. The count is at most s times the rate at the start of the sentence and at least s times the rate at its end; the same sentence served one period later prevents no more; and, net of replacement, the estimate from the rate at the start is still an upper bound. The usual constant-rate estimate therefore overstates what a sentence buys under both assumptions. See proof("incapr").

Usage

incapr(lam, t0, s, r = 0)

Arguments

lam

Offending rates by career age, lam[1] at age 0: non-negative numbers that never increase.

t0

The career age at which the sentence starts: a whole number from 0, with t0 + s at most length(lam) - 1.

s

The sentence in periods: a whole number from 1.

r

The replacement share: one number from 0 to 1.

Value

A named numeric vector: prev (crimes prevented), net (net of replacement), upper (s * lam at age t0), lower (s * lam at age t0 + s) and later (crimes prevented by the same sentence from age t0 + 1).

References

Shinnar, S. and Shinnar, R. (1975). The effects of the criminal justice system on the control of crime: a quantitative approach. Law and Society Review, 9(4), 581-611. doi:10.2307/3053340

Examples

incapr(lam = c(12, 10, 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 2, 1), t0 = 2, s = 3, r = 0.25)
#>  prev   net upper lower later 
#> 19.00 14.25 24.00 12.00 15.00
